added.name: Bayworks
added.long_description:
Bayworks is building the intelligence that runs automotive operations.

Over 1 million cars drive in for service every day in the US, but the industry is short 250,000 technicians who can fix them. 

Bayworks starts in the service bay, helps technicians repair vehicles faster, and turns every repair captured into intelligence to run operations autonomously.

added.name: Faraday
added.long_description:
Industrial enterprises still rely on people to coordinate disconnected software and machines, with critical knowledge held by a few experienced employees. 

Faraday builds self-improving systems that take on this operational work. We connect to existing software and machines and build training and evaluation environments around each company’s workflows and data.

Continuous learning turns each company’s expertise into a compounding asset. Completed work, corrections, and employee feedback improve the agents, and those improvements carry into future jobs. The business preserves its knowledge while becoming more capable over time.

As these agents take on more workflows, Faraday will be the shared runtime coordinating work between humans, agents, and robots across the business.
added.one_liner: Industrial AI coordinating humans, agents, and machines

long_description.before:
The best investments come from conviction, and conviction comes from understanding a market deeply: its customers, its competitors, and where it's heading.

Today that understanding is slow and expensive to build. Reaching the right people takes weeks, a commercial study costs $300k+, and each one starts from scratch.

LATO does this research end-to-end, combining public data and the fund's own knowledge with first-hand interviews of a market's consumers, experts, and operators. 

This research grounds a simulation of the market to predict how market participants behave.
long_description.after:
LATO is the agent-native research and simulation system that lets investors and companies test any thesis. Funds managing $400bn+ use LATO, including General Atlantic, Hg, Generation, NEA and Verdane, along with their portfolio companies.

We’re backed by leading funds including Y Combinator, Air Street Capital and Axiom Partners. Our angels include Paul Graham and co-founders of Vercel, ElevenLabs, Snowflake and Rogo. LATO was founded by a former private equity investor and an AI/ML engineer.

long_description.before:
Production agents handle many different customer workflows. Currently, when one handles a situation badly, an engineer reads the trace and patches the prompt. The next situation needs another exception. Soon, improving the agent becomes a recurring engineering job, and the prompt keeps growing.

Mirrors finds patterns in past runs. Engineers review guidance for a specific situation and preview where it would apply. Mirrors then delivers that guidance while the agent works, inside the team’s existing setup. The team can check whether the change improved the outcome.

We’re building Mirrors for engineering teams running customer-facing agents across varied workflows, so they can improve behavior without hardcoding every lesson in the global prompt.
long_description.after:
Production AI agents keep making the same mistakes. The usual fix is another line in the system prompt. Over time, the agent carries instructions for dozens of situations, even when it's doing something simple, and every correction becomes another thing to maintain.

Mirrors helps developers maintain production agents by turning recurring mistakes into targeted corrections. Mirrors surfaces recurring mistakes across your production runs. You write a correction, choose the situations where it applies, and preview which past conversations it would have reached. Once activated, Mirrors adds it to your agent only in those situations. You can then compare outcomes with and without the correction to see whether it helped. Unlike skills, the agent doesn't decide what to load. The scope you set does.

Corrections live in one place, scoped to the right accounts and workflows. Mirrors connects through an SDK and works with any agent framework, and your application keeps control of its model calls and tools.

We're building Mirrors for engineering teams running customer-facing agents.

one_liner.before: Fix recurring agent mistakes with real-time guidance
one_liner.after: Fix recurring AI agent mistakes with real-time guidance

long_description.before:

We've found and fixed dozens of previously unknown vulnerabilities (0-days) in government software across multiple countries and in software powering more than 3 billion devices. Today we work with EY (Ernst & Young), leading tech companies and defense organizations.

Our AI agents hack into any software, verify every vulnerability they find, and ship the fix autonomously. They run 24/7 across the full stack, from web apps and dependencies down to operating systems and the Linux kernel.

long_description.before: Graphide (YC F26) is a code editor that maps your codebase into a graph so you can see what your agents are building. Agents now write code faster than anyone can read it, and a line by line diff doesn't show what actually changed in the system. Graphide keeps a live graph of the modules, classes, functions, etc. how they connect, and what each agent is touching as it works. Graphide then checks their changes against your architecture, making sure your agents are implementing what you had in mind.
long_description.after:
Coding agents now write more code than teams can check, making verification pipelines the new bottleneck. Graphide builds that verification, starting with CI.

Graphide CI runs faster and cheaper because we own both the hardware and the optimizations and configs that run on it, which lets us do what owning only one could not. A graph of the codebase runs only the tests each change can reach, and always-on agents tune machines, caches and test splits together, around the clock. Optionally, we also patch the tests themselves with our own libraries so they run faster. We have seen most of our customers cut CI time 80-90% compared to their existing setups.

Our PR review agent then runs the old and new code in a live environment, finding bugs and proving them by writing tests, as well as analyzing synthetic and production data through the PR before it merges. The first 150 reviews are free.

Graphide verifies the code agents write.

one_liner.before: A graph based IDE for when agents program faster than you can read
one_liner.after: CI 10–20× faster than GitHub runners, for teams who ship with agents.

long_description.before:
Sutrix turns messy data from EHRs, clinical notes, wearables, and surveys into clean, study-ready datasets allowing hospital research teams' to deliver tailored patient care faster.

Before a clinical study can start, research staff spend weeks pulling patient data from disconnected systems like the EHR, REDCap, and wearable platforms, reading notes chart by chart, and reconciling conflicting entries in spreadsheets. Sutrix automates that work by deploying AI systems within each team’s own environment, linking patient records across sources, applying the study's rules, and flagging unclear cases for staff to review.

Paying research teams at 10+ institutions cut data prep by 80% going from months per study to weeks.

We're brothers who've built together for 4 years. We first solved this problem doing forward-deployed work at HSS, where we built an injury surveillance system now used by 700+ teams. Ritvik's clinical research at HSS and Emory showed us every research team has the same bottleneck. Supratik previously founded Kairo (a16z Speedrun, exited) and built production AI agents at Amazon.

long_description.before:
Traditional cloud infrastructure was built to run a single app for many users. Agents work differently. Each one needs its own isolated machine to write software on the fly, run tools and act on its own for hours or weeks. And everything it produces has to persist between sessions.

Superserve gives every agent and RL rollout its own virtual machine that starts in under 50ms. Machines start from templates with your repo and dependencies already loaded, pause with memory and files intact at zero compute cost, and resume or fork from that exact state. You can run docker, databases, browsers or any services on these VMs. 

API keys stay outside the machine and egress rules control what agents can reach.

For teams building coding agents, autonomous workers, or eval and training environments, that means elastic infrastructure with no servers or warm pools to manage, and control over what every agent can reach and which credentials it can see. 

We run over 100K machines (as of Oct 2026) every week for world-class teams, including Lindy, and Y Combinator itself.
long_description.after:
Superserve gives every AI agent its own computer in the cloud. Each one is an isolated VM that starts in under 50ms, sleeps between turns, and picks up exactly where it left off, for hours, weeks or indefinitely.

Traditional cloud infrastructure was built to run one app for many users. Agents flip that. Each agent needs its own isolated machine where it can write and run code, use tools and work on its own for long stretches. Everything it produces has to persist the whole time, the way your laptop keeps your work.

That means agent computers have to be stateful, secure and cheap to run. For agents that talk to customers, they also have to start, sleep and wake almost instantly.

Fast - Machines start in under 50ms, either cold or from a template with your repo and dependencies already loaded. You don't need to keep a pool of servers running and waiting.

Persistent - Paused machines keep their full memory and disk state at zero compute cost. They can resume or fork from that exact state. Pausing and resuming is fast enough that a machine can sleep between inference calls and wake on the next turn. Agents can run Docker, databases, browsers or any other service inside.

Secure - Every machine is a microVM with its own kernel. You can program the rules for what traffic can come in and go out, and they're enforced at the network boundary where the agent can't reach them. API secrets are handled at the network layer too, so they never enter the machine. Every action is logged for audits.

Teams building coding agents, autonomous workers, and eval or RL training environments use Superserve to give every agent session or rollout its own machine, with no infrastructure to manage.

We run 100K+ machines every week for teams including Lindy and Y Combinator.

long_description.before:
Hundred is an automated inspection system for the components that make up consumer devices like phones, smartwatches, and laptops. Hundred helps factories cut waste and prevent line-down issues by catching sub-100µm cosmetic defects before parts reach the assembly line. 

In the consumer electronics industry, designs change so fast that traditional machine vision can't keep up, forcing factories to rely on manual inspection, literally people checking parts under microscopes to sort out bad parts. Human inspectors miss roughly 15% of defects, and a single bad part can turn a finished device into scrap. Hundred is replacing manual inspection with an imaging rig that scans an entire shipping tray of parts at once. 

The Hundred rig blocks ambient light and uses varied controlled lighting configurations to detect defects smaller than 100µm on a range of materials. The controlled environment means Hundred only needs to scan a single good part before it can find defects, categorize them, and assess their severity accurately.

Defects cost U.S. discrete manufacturers $45 billion a year, a problem Hundred's CEO, Erica, saw firsthand as a mechanical engineer designing devices at Meta, Google, and Magic Leap. She met Imani, Hundred's CPO, at Columbia University's admitted-students day in 2017 and Imani went on to spend five years at Twitch building software that handles billions of requests a day. Erica later met Iris, Hundred's CTO, in the Bay Area. Iris worked as a quant at Citadel before pivoting to study at Imperial College London where she researched machine learning on 3D meshes and other structured data. Together, they're building Hundred because manual inspection shouldn't still exist in 2026.
